name: NGC 1277 (Hubble)
blurb: NGC 1277, a lenticular galaxy in the Perseus Cluster, seen by Hubble.
label: ngc1277-hubble
story: A galaxy that stopped growing long ago, dubbed a relic of the early universe. Its globular star clusters are mostly metal-rich, a sign it never grew by swallowing neighboring galaxies.

claims.text: NGC 1277 is a member of the Perseus Cluster
Dubbed a relic of the early universe
Its globular clusters are mostly red and metal-rich
Program 14215 targets NGC 1277 as a relic galaxy unaltered since early assembly, testing whether its globular clusters show it never accreted others
Called a 'red and dead' galaxy; almost entirely missing blue globular clusters, suggesting it never absorbed neighboring galaxies
